Two quick presses of the power key turn the torch on or off, even while the phone is locked. While it is on, the lock screen says so; press that line to turn it off. Needs \"Glance on the lock screen\" switched on in Accessibility.

Shows today\'s events, the weather and what is unread on the lock screen, from the apps that hand it lines, and how many notifications the apps you choose have waiting. Without Datebook, it can read today\'s events itself if you turn that on. It reads the lock screen only to see where its own items end and whether the PIN pad is up, and it has no network access.
Today\'s events, the weather, pinned notes, the next dose and what is unread, on the lock screen, so the day can be seen without unlocking the phone. Press a line to open its app.
Glance has no internet access, so nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is collected about you. It keeps only your choices on this phone: the order, the apps you chose and its switches.

It puts on the lock screen what Datebook, Sky and your other apps hand it, and the phone\'s lock does not hide it: anyone holding the phone can read today\'s events, the weather and what is unread. Each app\'s own switch decides what it hands over.

With notification access on, it reads the notifications of the apps you choose to count them, and what they say only if you turn on Show what they say. Without Datebook, it reads today\'s events from Mudita\'s Calendar and, if you allow calendar access, the phone\'s other calendars. As an accessibility service it reads the lock screen only to find where its own items end. With Power pressed twice on, it notes when the screen goes on and off to switch the torch, and keeps nothing of it. Ring for calls only adds a Do Not Disturb rule of its own. It hands the panel\'s lines to inkOS:wndr\'s home screen and to no other app.
There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking.
